navigate.description: Navigate to a URL in the current tab, or open it in a new tab with new_tab=True

new_tab.description: If True, open the URL in a new tab instead of navigating the current tab
new_tab.title: New Tab

click.description: Click an element by its ID from the DOM state. Use index (from the DOM tree) or element_id (a backend node id from find_elements with return_node_ids=True).

index.description: ID of the element to click, shown in brackets in the DOM tree. Provide exactly one of index / element_id.
index.title: Index

element_id.description: Stable backend node id from find_elements(return_node_ids=True); an alternative to index (same resolution path). Provide exactly one of index / element_id.
element_id.title: Element Id

input_text.description: Type text into an input element identified by index (from the DOM tree) or element_id (a backend node id from find_elements with return_node_ids=True).

index.description: ID of the element to type into, shown in brackets in the DOM tree. Provide exactly one of index / element_id.
index.title: Index

element_id.description: Stable backend node id from find_elements(return_node_ids=True); an alternative to index (same resolution path). Provide exactly one of index / element_id.
element_id.title: Element Id

text.description: Text to type into the element
text.title: Text

clear.description: Whether to clear existing text first
clear.title: Clear

scroll.description: Scroll the page up or down by a number of increments

amount.description: Number of viewport-heights to scroll (1-10). Check the scroll info on scrollable elements in the DOM tree (e.g. '3.4 pages below') to judge how much remains before scrolling.
amount.title: Amount

search.description: Search the web via a search engine (baidu/google/bing/duckduckgo; default baidu). Navigates to the results page

query.description: Search query to type into the search engine
query.title: Query

engine.description: Search engine: baidu (default, works in China), google, bing, or duckduckgo
engine.title: Engine

extract.description: Extract specific information from the current page as clean markdown (via an LLM). Paginate large pages with start_from_char; dedupe across calls with already_collected.

query.description: What information to extract from the current page. Be specific: name the fields/items and any filtering criteria. (Equivalent to browser-use `query`.)
query.title: Query

extract_links.description: If True, preserve <a href> URLs in the source markdown. Set False for text-only extraction.
extract_links.title: Extract Links

extract_images.description: If True, preserve URLs in the source markdown.
extract_images.title: Extract Images

start_from_char.description: Character offset to resume extraction from (for paginating large pages). Default 0 = start at the beginning. Use the offset reported by a previous truncated extract call to continue.
start_from_char.title: Start From Char

already_collected.description: Items already extracted (dedupe across pages/chunks). Pass prior results (as text) and the model will skip exact duplicates. Optional.
already_collected.title: Already Collected

send_keys.description: Send keyboard shortcuts or key combinations

keys.description: Key combination or text to send. Combos use '+': 'Control+a', 'Shift+T', 'Alt+F4'. Named keys: 'Enter', 'Tab', 'Escape', 'ArrowUp', 'F5', etc. Plain text (e.g. 'hello') is typed character by character.
keys.title: Keys

switch_tab.description: Switch to a different browser tab by tab ID

tab_id.description: Tab ID (last 4 characters) to switch to
tab_id.title: Tab Id

tab_id.description: Tab ID (last 4 characters) to close. Empty string closes the current tab.
tab_id.title: Tab Id

wait.description: Wait for a specified number of seconds

go_back.description: Navigate back to the previous page in history

find_elements.description: Query DOM elements by CSS selector (zero LLM cost, instant). Returns matching elements with tag, text, and attributes. Use attributes=['href','src'] to extract specific attributes (src/href resolve to absolute URLs). max_results caps the returned list; the total count is always reported. Use to explore page structure, count items, get links/attributes.

selector.description: CSS selector to query elements (e.g. "table tr", "a.link", "div.product")
selector.title: Selector

attributes.description: Specific attributes to extract (e.g. ["href", "src", "class"]). If not set, returns tag and text only. src/href are resolved to absolute URLs.
attributes.title: Attributes

max_results.description: Maximum elements to return (total count is always reported even when truncated).
max_results.title: Max Results

offset.description: 0-based index of the first element to return (for paginating large result sets; total is always the full count across all roots including shadow DOM / same-origin iframes).
offset.title: Offset

include_text.description: Include text content of each element
include_text.title: Include Text

first_only.description: Return only the first matching element; total still reports the full count so you know there are more.
first_only.title: First Only

include_geometry.description: Add per-element getBoundingClientRect() {x,y,w,h} and a stable visibility flag (checks ancestor display/visibility/opacity + non-zero size). Default off to avoid overhead.
include_geometry.title: Include Geometry

return_node_ids.description: Return stable backend node ids usable directly as click/input_text `index` (uses DOM.performSearch — heavier, one CDP round-trip per element; no text). Offset applies to the document-order match list.
return_node_ids.title: Return Node Ids

find_text.description: Scroll to and highlight the nth visible match of text on the page

text.description: Text to search for on the page
text.title: Text

nth.description: Which match to scroll to, 1-based (default: 1st). The echo reports total/visible counts so the caller can increment to navigate matches.
nth.title: Nth

case_sensitive.description: Case-sensitive match (default: case-insensitive, like Ctrl+F). Aligns with search_page.
case_sensitive.title: Case Sensitive

highlight.description: Highlight style: box=element outline (default), selection=native blue text selection (best-effort, Chromium-only), none=off.
highlight.title: Highlight

screenshot.description: Take a screenshot with optional format, quality (jpeg), clip region, or full page. Saves to save_path if given.

ScreenshotClipParams.description: Viewport rectangle for a clipped screenshot, in CSS pixels.
ScreenshotClipParams.title: ScreenshotClipParams

format.description: Image format. 'jpeg' supports quality; 'png' is lossless.
format.title: Format

full_page.description: Capture the full scrollable page instead of the viewport.
full_page.title: Full Page

save_path.description: Optional file path to save the screenshot bytes to disk.
save_path.title: Save Path

save_as_pdf.description: Save the current page as a PDF. Supports paper_format (letter/legal/a4/a3/tabloid), landscape, scale (0.1-2.0), print_background.

path.description: File path to save the PDF (parent dirs auto-created).
path.title: Path

dropdown_options.description: Get all options from a dropdown element: native <select>, role=combobox, role=listbox, or custom dropdown

index.description: ID of the select element, shown in brackets in the DOM tree
index.title: Index

select_dropdown.description: Select an option in a dropdown element (native <select>, role=combobox, role=listbox, or custom dropdown). Pass the dropdown's index — do not click it first. For <select multiple>, pass all wanted options at once as values=[...]

index.description: ID of the select element, shown in brackets in the DOM tree
index.title: Index

value.description: Option value to select (single option). Each call REPLACES the selection.
value.title: Value

values.description: For <select multiple> only: ALL wanted option values in ONE call — replaces the whole selection (repeated single-value calls keep only the last one)
values.title: Values

upload_file.description: Upload a file to a file input element. Do NOT click the input or an upload button first — upload_file sets the file directly without opening the OS file picker

index.description: ID of the file input element (or its labeled upload area / dropzone), shown in brackets in the DOM tree
index.title: Index

path.description: Path to the file to upload
path.title: Path

write_file.description: Write UTF-8 text to a local file (parent directories are auto-created). Default is overwrite: the file's previous content is fully replaced. Set append=True to add to the end of an existing file instead (it is created if missing). trailing_newline (default True) ensures the content ends with exactly one newline — no-op if it already does; set leading_newline=True only when appending to a file you know lacks a trailing newline, to separate the new content. Prefer replace_file for in-place edits to a small region of a large file you have already read.

path.description: File path to write to (parent directories are auto-created).
path.title: Path

content.description: Text content to write (UTF-8 by default; see encoding).
content.title: Content

append.description: If True, append to the end of an existing file instead of overwriting it. Default False overwrites the entire file.
append.title: Append

trailing_newline.description: If True (default), ensure the written content ends with exactly one newline (no-op if it already does).
trailing_newline.title: Trailing Newline

leading_newline.description: If True, prepend a newline before the content (useful when appending to a file that lacks a trailing newline).
leading_newline.title: Leading Newline

encoding.description: Text encoding to write with (default UTF-8). Set e.g. 'latin-1' or 'cp936' for legacy files; the byte-count echo reflects this encoding.
encoding.title: Encoding

newline.description:
Python open() newline translation mode (default '' = no translation; 
/
 written as-is). Set '
' to force CRLF output, None to translate 
 to the OS native line ending (
 on Windows). Distinct from trailing_newline/leading_newline, which only add/remove a 
 in the content.
newline.title: Newline

read_file.description: Read content from a local text (UTF-8) or PDF/DOCX file; paginate large files with offset/limit.

path.description: Path to a local file to read: UTF-8 text by default (see encoding), or PDF/DOCX for text extraction.
path.title: Path

encoding.description: Text encoding to decode with (default UTF-8). Set e.g. 'latin-1' or 'cp936' for legacy files.
encoding.title: Encoding

newline.description:
Python open() newline mode (default '' = no translation, preserves 
 byte-for-byte). Set None for universal-newline (collapses 
 /  to 
); other values do not translate on a full-file read.
newline.title: Newline

offset.description: 0-based character offset to start reading at (for paginating files larger than the effective read window; pair with the truncation footer's 'use offset=N to continue').
offset.title: Offset

limit.description: Max characters to return from this read (default: the effective read window = min(read_file_max_chars, LLM display cap) minus a footer reserve). Use with offset to page through very large files.
limit.title: Limit

replace_file.description: Replace occurrences of text inside an existing local file, in place. By default performs a case-sensitive literal substring replace of every non-overlapping occurrence (phase-1 behavior preserved). Set regex=True to treat 'old' as a Python regex (then 'new' supports backreferences), or case_sensitive=False for case-insensitive matching. count limits replacements to the first N (default: all). expected_count guards against typos: if the file does not contain exactly that many matches it is left unchanged and an error is returned. backup=True first copies the original to <path>.bak. old must be non-empty; zero matches returns 'no occurrences' rather than silently succeeding. Prefer this over write_file for small edits to a large file you have already read.

path.description: Path to an existing local file to edit in place.
path.title: Path

old.description: Text to find. A literal substring by default (case-sensitive); set regex=True to treat it as a Python regular expression. Must be non-empty.
old.title: Old

new.description: Replacement text (literal; may be empty to delete matches). In regex mode this is an re.sub replacement template and supports backreferences (\1, \g<name>); escape backslashes for literal paths.
new.title: New

encoding.description: Text encoding to read/write with (default UTF-8). Set e.g. 'latin-1' or 'cp936' for legacy files.
encoding.title: Encoding

newline.description: Python open() newline mode (default '' = no translation, preserves original line endings byte-for-byte). Set None for universal-newline translation on read.
newline.title: Newline

regex.description: When True, treat 'old' as a Python regular expression (re.sub semantics, including backreference expansion \1 / \g<name> in 'new'; escape backslashes for literal paths). When False (default), 'old' is a literal substring.
regex.title: Regex

case_sensitive.description: When True (default), match case-sensitively. When False, match case-insensitively regardless of regex mode. Note: defaults to True (unlike search_page's False) to preserve replace_file's historical case-sensitive behavior.
case_sensitive.title: Case Sensitive

count.description: Maximum number of occurrences to replace, from the top of the file. None (default) replaces all; a positive integer replaces only the first N (or fewer if the file has fewer matches).
count.title: Count

expected_count.description: If set, the file must contain exactly this many matches for the operation to proceed; on mismatch the file is left UNCHANGED and an error is returned (typo-guard against 0 or unexpectedly-many replacements). Compared against the TOTAL match count, before the 'count' limit is applied.
expected_count.title: Expected Count

backup.description: When True, copy the original (pre-edit) file to <path>.bak before replacing (shutil.copy2 metadata retained). Default False; .bak is overwritten if it exists.
backup.title: Backup

evaluate.description: Execute arbitrary JavaScript in the page and return the result. Wrap in an IIFE with try-catch so errors become return values; use only browser APIs (no Node.js). Supports async (await / fetch). Result is normalized to a string (objects -> JSON). Escape hatch when find_elements / search_page / click cannot express the need. Avoid backslash escapes in the code (they get mangled in transport): for newlines/tabs inside regex use String.fromCharCode(10)/String.fromCharCode(9) instead of \n/\t.

code.description: JavaScript to execute in the page. The code runs as a SCRIPT BODY — a top-level `return` is a SyntaxError unless wrapped, so use an IIFE: ((function(){try{...}catch(e){return 'Error: '+e.message}})()). Contrast: with `args`/`elements` the code IS wrapped as function(...a){ ... } and then MUST `return`. Use ONLY browser APIs (document, window, fetch); NO Node.js APIs. Return a primitive or a JSON-serializable object/array. Keep output small. Keep CODE short (< ~300 chars) — longer nested code tends to lose brace balance; split into several evaluate calls instead.
code.title: Code

await_promise.description: Await a returned Promise (default True; needed for await fetch(...)). Set False for fire-and-forget / strictly synchronous code.
await_promise.title: Await Promise

timeout_ms.description: Per-call CDP execution timeout in ms, clamped to [1, 300000]. Default None → 30000 (project default). Larger for long fetches, smaller to fail fast. Only applies when no args/elements are given.
timeout_ms.title: Timeout Ms

user_gesture.description: Run as a user gesture — required by some APIs (fullscreen, certain clipboard / pointer-lock calls). No-op for most code.
user_gesture.title: User Gesture

args.description: Optional JSON arguments injected as a[0], a[1], ... Your code is wrapped as function(...a){ ... } so it MUST `return` a value. Eliminates string-concat injection: pass values as JSON, reference them as a[i]. Example: args=['.btn'] with code `return document.querySelector(a[0]).disabled`.
args.title: Args

elements.description: Backend node ids (index/element_id from get_state or find_elements(return_node_ids=True)) of elements to inject as handles e[0], e[1], ... When present, code is wrapped as function(...a, ...e){ ... } (JSON args first, element handles last) and MUST `return`. Lets JS act on the exact node click/input_text operate on, without re-querying. Example: elements=[42] with code `return e[0].value`.
elements.title: Elements

return_element_ids.description: If True, a returned DOM node is resolved to its backend node id (usable as `index`/`element_id` for click/input_text) and reported. Expects the code to `return` a single element (e.g. `return document.querySelector('form')`). Only the first returned node is resolved; non-node returns fall back to normal normalization.
return_element_ids.title: Return Element Ids

frame.description: Backend node id of an iframe element to execute inside (cross-origin safe). Default None → top document. When set, the call runs in that iframe's context (attached via Target.attachToTarget). Use when the parent cannot reach a cross-origin iframe's document. Same-origin iframes do NOT need this — just reference `iframe.contentDocument` in your code.
frame.title: Frame

extract_images.description: If True, scan the result text for `data:image/...;base64,...` URIs, collect them into ActionResult.metadata['images'], and replace each in the returned text with a short placeholder ([image 1], [image 2], ...) to avoid bloating context. Default False.
extract_images.title: Extract Images

search_page.description: Search page text for a pattern (like grep). Zero LLM cost, instant. Returns matches with surrounding context, element path, and a total count; paginate large result sets with offset. Traverses same-origin iframes and open shadow roots. Set regex=True for regex patterns; use css_scope to search within a section; search_attributes=True to also match href/value/etc. Read-only — does not scroll or highlight (use find_text for that).

query.description: Text or regex pattern to search for within the current page
query.title: Query

regex.description: Treat query as a regex (default: literal text match).
regex.title: Regex

context_chars.description: Characters of surrounding context per match.
context_chars.title: Context Chars

css_scope.description: CSS selector to limit search scope (e.g. 'div#main'). Selector not matching anything is an error.
css_scope.title: Css Scope

max_results.description: Maximum matches to return (total count is always reported even when truncated).
max_results.title: Max Results

offset.description: 0-based index of the first match to return (for paginating large result sets; total is always the full count).
offset.title: Offset

search_attributes.description: Also search element attribute values (href / value / data-* etc). Returns a separate attribute_matches list; offset applies to text matches only.
search_attributes.title: Search Attributes

read_grid.description: Read structured rows from the page's tables and data grids — UI-component grids, legacy AJAX grids, plain HTML tables, and report result tables. Rows come back keyed by column header (plain/report tables and legacy grids) or by data-source field name (UI-component grids — check the returned keys before passing fields). For tables, adjacent numeric columns cannot be confused — use this instead of reading table values off the DOM snapshot by cell position. When the table has a Total/合计 row, it is returned as footer together with computed per-column sums (totals-check) for cross-checking. Bypasses row-render freezes; returns JSON rows plus metadata (total_records, sorting, active filters). Pass sorting='field desc' for top-N/latest queries — never assume row order. Read-only data channel: does NOT update the page UI (filter chips) — tasks graded on visible filter state must use the Filters panel.

namespace.description: Grid namespace, e.g. 'sales_order_grid' / 'product_listing'. Omit to auto-detect from the current page (first non-notification UI-component grid data source).
namespace.title: Namespace

filters.description: Grid filters applied server-side, e.g. {'status':'complete'} or {'qty':{'from':2,'to':3}}. Replaces current filters (leftover bookmark filters are cleared first). Pass {} to read unfiltered.
filters.title: Filters

search.description: Fulltext keyword for the grid's search box (replaces current).
search.title: Search

sorting.description: '<field> <asc|desc>', e.g. 'created_at desc'. REQUIRED for top-N / latest / max queries — grid row order is otherwise NOT guaranteed.
sorting.title: Sorting

page_size.description: Rows per page for this read (server-side paging; use 1000+ to read all).
page_size.title: Page Size

fields.description: Row fields to return, e.g. ['entity_id','increment_id','created_at','status']. Omit for all grid columns.
fields.title: Fields

fresh.description: True (default): clear leftover server-side bookmark filters/search before applying the given params — grids inherit filter state from previous sessions. False: apply on top of the current state.
fresh.title: Fresh

group_count.description: Field name to aggregate on, e.g. 'billing_name': returns per-value row counts computed in Python over the rows this call returned (no context tallying; the decisive tool for count-per-X questions). Watch the appended warnings — 'counted X of total Y' means page through for exact totals; legacy/DOM channels are page-local (current page/pageSize rows only, no total reported). Works on every channel. Pass fields=[that field] to slim the returned rows. If counts come back '(missing)', the field name is not present in the rows (legacy/DOM channels use display-name headers).
group_count.title: Group Count

done.description: Signal that the task is complete and stop the agent. Must be the only action in the step. Provide a final summary of what was accomplished; set success=False if any requirement was unmet or could not be verified.

text.description: Final message to the user. ONLY report data you directly observed in page state, tool outputs, or screenshots during this session. Do NOT use training knowledge to fill gaps — if information was not found on the page, say so explicitly. Do NOT claim completion of steps from compacted_memory or prior session summaries unless you explicitly verified them yourself. If uncertain whether a prior step completed, say so explicitly. Must be non-empty.
text.title: Text

success.description: Whether the task was completed successfully. Set to False if any stated requirement was unmet, the page did not contain the expected data, or a step could not be verified. Leave True only when every requirement was directly confirmed this session. If any part of your data is incomplete or still marked uncertain — a value with `?`, an unread gap, a partial tally — verify it first or set success=False.
success.title: Success

files_to_display.description: Absolute file paths to attach to the final result (downloads, saved reports, screenshots). Each must exist and be under an allowed read path; invalid paths are skipped with a warning. Shown as a short manifest in the summary.
files_to_display.title: Files To Display
